steps.what: Review the relevant patient context and select applicable approved prevention material using the clinical record system {OTHER} and {DOCS}; configure native links to current diet, activity and prevention texts, verifying their relevance.
outputs: selected prevention material and relevant patient context

steps.what: Discuss appropriate diet, activity, hygiene and prevention with the patient, adapt the advice to their condition and circumstances and check their understanding.
inputs: selected prevention material and relevant patient context
outputs: actual prevention advice and patient response

steps.what: Write the actual advice, relevant limitations and patient response in the clinical record system {OTHER}, then check the completed note against the consultation.
inputs: actual prevention advice and patient response

steps.what: Save the checked final prevention note in the clinical record system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure native links from the clinical record system {OTHER} to current approved prevention texts in {DOCS}. The cardiologist selects what applies, gives the actual advice and writes the actual consultation note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the current approved prevention material can require repeated document navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native clinical context links and document versions can shorten that lookup.
tasks.still_hard: Individual clinical limits, patient circumstances and understanding require conversation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when general prevention advice is inappropriate for this patient.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less material lookup; consultation and recording remain.

reach.learn: Separate general material from condition-specific dietary decisions.

evidence.claim: Clinical document links can expose current approved patient information without determining which advice applies.

assumptions: Boundary is an individual cardiovascular prevention consultation through its clinical note. Community sessions use their actual audience and approved public materials; they do not acquire a fictional patient record. Shares describe the individual case and are illustrative.

The cardiologist verifies patient/encounter identity, relevant condition and restrictions from existing clinical records, and selects document ID/version and language in s1. Missing context requires human clarification; no ambient recording or inferred restrictions. Actual advice and response are captured manually in s3 with full effort.

Native links precede code. Only repeated material navigation loses time, not clinical record reading, clinical selection, conversation or note writing. If no repeated material lookup occurs, saving is zero.

The ordinary completed-note check at the end of s3 supplies the requested s4 commit gate without an additional self-approval activity. Changes require rechecking; the one-share save is fully retained. No separate patient send is introduced.
unknowns: Actual lookup frequency and existing links
research_questions: Can current-version links reduce material navigation without obscuring clinical limitations?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Native links remove 20% of the 15-hour preparation share: 3 gross hours less 0.5 upkeep. Zero if already linked or no repeated lookup. All conversation, actual note writing and save retain full time.

tasks.short: Answer an existing patient portal health question

steps.what: Read the actual questions patients have about their health and well-being in the clinical portal {OTHER}, clarify their meaning where needed and determine whether they require immediate clinical attention rather than a routine written response.
outputs: understood question and clinician-selected response route

steps.what: Review the relevant clinical history and current approved information in the clinical record system {OTHER} and {DOCS}, deciding what can be answered from the available evidence.
inputs: understood question and clinician-selected response route

steps.what: Draft the written reply in the clinical portal {OTHER}; configure native approved-text snippets for repeated explanatory passages while the cardiologist writes the patient-specific explanation and limitations.

Check the completed reply against the actual question, clinical record and source text, including negation, uncertainty, individual applicability, clarity and the correct recipient; revise it before release.
outputs: checked final patient reply and recipient

steps.what: Save the checked final patient reply in the clinical portal {OTHER}.
inputs: checked final patient reply and recipient

steps.what: Send the checked final reply to its verified patient recipient through the clinical portal {OTHER}.
inputs: checked final patient reply and recipient

tasks.design: Configure approved-text snippets in the existing clinical portal {OTHER} for common explanatory passages. The cardiologist reads the actual question, determines the response, writes the personal explanation and checks the complete reply before separate save and send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routine written answers may repeatedly type the same approved explanations.
tasks.enabler_now: Native snippets reuse fixed approved passages while preserving physician editing.
tasks.still_hard: Unclear symptoms, incomplete history and reassurance require clinical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a written answer would be unsafe or would fail to address the patient's concern.

ambition.what: No autonomous patient response or triage.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated wording in existing portal correspondence, with clinical assessment unchanged.

reach.learn: Check clarity without changing the clinical meaning.

evidence.claim: Clinical portal snippets can reuse approved explanatory passages while leaving patient-specific drafting and release to the clinician.

assumptions: Boundary is an already existing written portal-question case, not converting all in-person questions into new correspondence. This is separate from the prevention consultation in task 22690. Shares are illustrative and not a claim about all cardiologist work.

The patient produces the actual question in the existing portal. The clinical record supplies verified patient and encounter IDs and history; approved sources supply text ID, version and language. The cardiologist selects applicable passages and writes the personal answer in s2-s3. Missing context prompts manual clarification, fully retained. No structured symptoms or answer are assumed to exist without that work.

Native snippets precede any model. The reduction is repeated typing of genuinely reusable passages, not reasoning or consultation. A model is unnecessary for inserting fixed text. If no repeated wording exists or snippets already exist, no saving follows.

s4 is the ordinary check of the completed reply and recipient. It binds both final actions; edits invalidate the check. Save and send are each one fully retained share. Existing urgent clinical pathways remain human decisions and are not automated.
unknowns: Existing snippet configuration and approved content governance
research_questions: How much reply drafting repeats approved wording while patient-specific reasoning remains unchanged?

tasks.short: Calculate valve area from verified echocardiographic measurements

steps.what: Review the actual echocardiographic measurement traces and their quality in the echocardiography workstation {OTHER}, confirming patient, study, beat selection and relevant measurement units.
Select the clinically applicable valve-area calculation method and its required measurements, confirming that the source measurements satisfy that method's assumptions.
outputs: selected method and accepted measurement inputs

steps.what: Prepare the valve-area calculation in the echocardiography workstation {OTHER}; configure native calculation fields to reference the accepted measurements instead of re-entering them, then verify field mapping, units and calculated output.
inputs: selected method and accepted measurement inputs

steps.what: Check the completed valve-area result against the source traces, selected method and clinical plausibility, documenting method limitations and resolving discrepancies before finalising the result entry.
inputs: selected method and accepted measurement inputs

steps.what: Save the checked final valve-area result entry in the echocardiography workstation {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure native calculation fields in the echocardiography workstation {OTHER} to reuse accepted source measurements. The cardiologist retains measurement-quality assessment, method selection and completed-result checking.
tasks.previous_blocker: Accepted measurements may be re-entered into calculation fields despite already existing in the study.
tasks.enabler_now: Native measurement references and unit-aware fields can remove repeated entry.
tasks.still_hard: Poor acquisition and invalid method assumptions cannot be repaired by arithmetic.
tasks.human_edge: Reject a precise-looking result when the underlying measurements are unsuitable.

ambition.what: No automatic diagnosis or treatment decision.

tasks.altitude: Less measurement re-entry; clinical accountability stays unchanged.

reach.learn: Preserve study, beat and method provenance.

evidence.claim: Echocardiography workstation calculations can reference explicit accepted measurements, while method validity remains a clinical judgement.

assumptions: Boundary starts with acquired study traces and ends with the stored valve-area result, not acquiring the examination or making a diagnosis. No acquisition saving is claimed. Shares are a conditional adoption scenario.

The existing examination producer supplies patient/study ID, trace and beat references, measurement name/value/unit and quality context. The cardiologist verifies these in s1 and selects the method and inputs in s2. Velocity alone is not presumed sufficient: for a continuity-based aortic calculation the accepted outflow dimension and relevant outflow and transvalvular velocity-time integrals must also exist. Missing or unsuitable inputs require manual clinical resolution; nothing is inferred.

Try existing approved native calculations first. Only repeated measurement entry and calculation preparation lose time; existing arithmetic runtime earns no saving. If measurements already populate the native calculation, savings are zero. Native configuration must preserve the approved method rather than introduce a new clinical formula.
The ordinary completed-result check in s4 supplies the requested s5 final-version commit gate with no added self-approval stage. Changes require rechecking; save retains one fully counted share.
unknowns: Actual repeated entry time and approved calculation methods
research_questions: Which accepted measurements still require manual re-entry into the native calculation?

incremental.description: Validate native measurement-field mappings after configuration changes.

approvals.approved_version: Final valve-area result entry checked at the end of s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Native references remove 40% of the 20-hour repeated calculation-preparation share: 8 gross hours less 1 upkeep. Zero where the workstation already populates those fields. Measurement review, method selection, final clinical check and save retain full time.

tasks.short: Compare cardiac dimensions with applicable reference standards

steps.what: Review actual chamber-size and wall-thickness measurements and source images in the echocardiography workstation {OTHER}, checking acquisition quality, study identity and required patient context.

Select applicable approved reference standards and prepare the dimension comparisons in the echocardiography workstation {OTHER}; configure native reference tables and explicit indexing fields, then check their applicability, units and displayed differences.
Interpret the comparisons with the images and clinical context, deciding which findings represent abnormalities and documenting uncertainty rather than equating a threshold flag with diagnosis.

Write the actual dimension interpretation in the existing study findings entry in the echocardiography workstation {OTHER}; check the completed wording, values, uncertainty and study references before saving.
Save the checked final cardiac-dimension findings entry in the echocardiography workstation {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure native reference tables and indexing fields in the echocardiography workstation {OTHER}. The cardiologist verifies applicability and images, interprets abnormality and writes the actual findings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dimension comparisons may require repeated reference-table lookup and manual indexing entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reference fields can display explicit comparisons against a selected, versioned standard.
tasks.still_hard: Image quality, method differences and patient context determine whether a comparison is meaningful.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a reference-range deviation from a clinically supported abnormal finding.
tasks.altitude: Less reference lookup and comparison preparation; interpretation stays with the cardiologist.

reach.learn: Preserve measurement method and reference-standard applicability.

evidence.claim: Native measurement tables can display explicit reference comparisons while clinical abnormality interpretation remains separate.

assumptions: Boundary is comparison and interpretation of chamber and wall dimensions through its existing study findings entry. This is distinct from the valve-area calculation in task 22692; neither measurement acquisition nor a whole examination report is counted twice. Shares are illustrative.

Existing study records supply patient/study ID, dimension name/value/unit, acquisition method/phase and required patient indexing context. The cardiologist verifies them in s1 and selects standard/version, applicable category and indexing method in s2. Manual entry and missing-field clarification remain counted. No demographic category, body size or normality is guessed.

Native reference configuration precedes custom code. Savings concern repeated lookup and numeric comparison only. Standard selection, result review, clinical interpretation and actual findings writing remain counted; existing automated comparison runtime earns no saving.

The ordinary final findings check in s4 binds the completed entry for s5 without an added approval activity. Changes invalidate it; the one-share save is fully retained. No external report release is added.
unknowns: Actual manual indexing and lookup burden
research_questions: Can the native display expose the chosen standard and missing indexing inputs rather than silently defaulting them?
